doc_name: Orchestra of the Age of Enlightenment
text: The Orchestra of the Age of Enlightenment (OAE) is a British period instrument orchestra with its headquarters at Acland Burghley School. It is the resident orchestra at Southbank Centre and Glyndebourne Festival Opera, and serves as Artistic Associate at Kings Place. The leadership is rotated among four musicians: Matthew Truscott, Kati Debretzeni, Huw Daniel, and Margaret Faultless. Formed in 1986 as a self-governing ensemble by a group of period instrumentalists, the OAE takes its name from the late 18th century, the historical period that forms the core of its repertoire. The orchestra does not have a principal conductor and instead selects conductors individually. The current Principal Artists are Sir Simon Rattle, Vladimir Jurowski, Iván Fischer, John Butt, Sir Mark Elder, and András Schiff. William Christie is Emeritus Conductor, as are the late Frans Brüggen, Sir Roger Norrington, and Sir Charles Mackerras. Other conductors who have worked with the OAE include Marin Alsop, Anu Tali, Yannick Nézet-Séguin, Sian Edwards, Edward Gardner, Suzi Digby, Robin Ticciati, Joanna Tomlinson, Philippe Herreweghe, Gustav Leonhardt, René Jacobs, Harry Bicket, Christopher Hogwood, Sigiswald Kuijken, Ivor Bolton, Monica Huggett, and Bruno Weil. Sir Martin Smith played a key role in establishing the OAE, securing private funding for its founding and serving on the Board for many years, and is now Life President. The OAE's ethos is democratic, with players actively guiding the artistic direction and having the right to join regardless of whether they are asked to play. Responsibility for concert planning lies with the Players' Artistic Committee, elected annually by members and also sitting on the OAE Board of Directors. An early mission statement stated the orchestra aimed to "Avoid the dangers implicit in:" The OAE's first concerts, held in June 1986 at Oxford's Town Hall and London's Queen Elizabeth Hall, were conducted by Sigiswald Kuijken and featured Telemann's Overture Suite, Rameau's Suite from Dardanus, Gossec's symphony, and Haydn's Symphony No. 83. The founding leaders were Catherine Mackintosh, Elizabeth Wallfisch, Alison Bury, and Margaret Faultless. The OAE's recurring season at Southbank Centre includes concerts at the Queen Elizabeth Hall and Royal Festival Hall. In May 2006, the OAE launched "The Night Shift," a series of informal late-night concerts, which has twice been nominated for a Royal Philharmonic Society Award for audience development. The Night Shift, established in 2006, presents classical music in a relaxed setting with performances of concise length, the allowance of alcoholic drinks, and the ability to clap and talk freely. More than 80% of its audience is under 35, and about 20% are attending a classical concert for the first time. In 2007, the OAE celebrated its 21st anniversary with a concert at the Royal Festival Hall, conducted by Norrington, Elder, Mackerras, and Jurowski respectively. That year, it won the RPS Ensemble award for its broad repertoire, advocacy of original instruments, pioneering education initiatives, and the artistry of its members. In July 2008, the OAE moved its headquarters to Kings Place in London, sharing office space with the London Sinfonietta. On 29 January 2010, The Night Shift made its first appearance at The Roundhouse in Camden. In August 2010, the OAE performed at the Royal Albert Hall during the BBC Proms, conducting Wagner's Tristan und Isolde (Act 2) and the Love Scene from Romeo and Juliet by Berlioz, with soloists Sarah Connolly, Ben Heppner, and Violeta Urmana. In September 2020, the OAE, led by Jonathan Cohen and featuring Nicola Benedetti, Rodolfo Richter, and Matthew Truscott, performed at the Royal Albert Hall during the BBC Proms, playing Vivaldi's Concerto in D major for two violins, Concerto in D minor for two violins, Concerto in A minor for two oboes, Handel's Concerto grosso in B flat major and Passacaglia from Radamisto, Charles Avison's Concerto grosso no. 5 in D minor, and Bach's Concerto in D minor for two violins. In September 2020, the OAE moved its headquarters to Acland Burghley Secondary School in Tufnell Park, Camden, where the administrative office, library, and recording studio are located on campus, and musicians use the school's Grade II listed assembly hall for rehearsals, workshops, and small performances. The partnership, initially underwritten by £120,000 from the Sainsbury family's Linbury Trust for three years, allows Burghley pupils to attend rehearsals and collaborate on artistic projects, such as exploring Rameau's music with the school's dance students. The OAE believes this presence will be transformational, improving academic performance, language skills, engagement with music, and even enhancing the orchestra's own playing, a model inspired by the Deutsche Kammerphilharmonie's project in Bremen, Germany. The OAE has toured extensively, including South America and the US in 2002 and South East Asia in autumn 2003. Its discography includes over fifty recordings from Henry Purcell to Verdi, featuring guest artists such as Lorraine Hunt Lieberson, Renée Fleming, Susan Graham, Andreas Scholl, Ian Bostridge, Elizabeth Wallfisch, Emanuel Ax, Thomas Hampson, Cecilia Bartoli, Gerald Finley, Bob van Asperen, Anner Bylsma, Viktoria Mullova, and Michael Chance. The OAE is highly active in school engagement, especially in the area around Kings Place, offering concerts, leading youth projects, and teaching children to play instruments. In the spring/summer of 2010, it ran a series of three concerts inspired by Monteverdi's Vespers for schools. The Ann and Peter Law OAE Experience is an apprenticeship scheme for young period instrumentalists, established in 2002 and the only such scheme with a period orchestra. It is consistently over-subscribed and offers participants mentorship from OAE musicians, rehearsal opportunities with guest conductors, performances with the OAE, and sometimes concerts as an ensemble.
